full_story_part2_c1.canonical_text: At the river, he stopped. The bridge was gone. Rain had turned the water brown and violent. He stepped back, ran, and threw himself into the flood. The current pulled him under. He fought toward the light, caught a branch, and dragged himself onto the far bank. Farther along, three men blocked the road. A knife flashed. Melos struck the man holding it with his walking stick and ran uphill, their shouts following him. By afternoon, every step hurt. Blood stained his feet. He fell beside a rock and tried to rise, but his legs would not obey. He could wait here. Someone might find him. He could go home. His friend would die. For one terrible moment, that seemed easier than getting up.
